messages.subject: plyr is case sensitive
messages.body_plain: I have noticed that plyr is case sensitive when doing join() and ddply(... summarize...). Is there an option to ignore case?
messages.body_snippet: I have noticed that plyr is case sensitive when doing join() and ddply(... summarize...). Is there an option to ignore case?

messages.subject: Re: plyr is case sensitive
messages.body_plain:
I tried to do this with dplyr and didn't get anywhere nice, perhaps others have better ideas.

df1 <- data.frame(PLTID = paste0(rep(LETTERS[1:3], each = 10),rep(1:10, times=3)), value1 = runif(30))
df2 <- data.frame(PlTiD = paste0(rep(LETTERS[1:3], each = 10),rep(1:10, times=3)), value2 = runif(30))

findColName <- function(df, x) {
grep(x ,names(df),ignore.case=TRUE,value=TRUE)
}

I can find the column names using grep and ignoring case, but the input to *_join() for by is by = c("a" = "b") which I can't seem to parse inline.

paste(findColName("pltid", df1), " = ", findColName("pltid", df2))
[1] "PLTID  =  PlTiD"

So, I did it the hard way with eval(parse()).

full_join_insensitive <- function(df1, df2, join) {

e <- paste("full_join(", as.character(bquote(df1)),  ", ", as.character(bquote(df2)), ", by = c('", findColName(df1, join), "' = '", findColName(df2, join), "'))", sep="")
eval(parse(text = e))
}

full_join_insensitive(df1, df2, "pltid")

HTH,
Brandon

Hi all,

this is probably really simple to answer: How can I use named do()
results. The help page lists an example using summary but how can I do
it without summary?

####################################################################
library(boot)
library(dplyr)

df <- rbind(data_frame(t=1:10, ts="A", dat=1:10),
            data_frame(t=1:10, ts="B", dat=101:110))

bsmean <- function(d, ind) {
    mean(d[ind])
}

bsdf <- group_by(df, ts) %>% do(bs=boot(.$dat, R=10, statistic=bsmean))
####################################################################

This yields:

Source: local data frame [2 x 2]
Groups: <by row>

     ts        bs
  (chr)     (chr)

2     B <S3:boot>

List of 1

<environment: 0x2283e38>

Hi:

dput() is a function that takes an R object as input and returns a
text-based representation of it that can be copied and pasted into
e-mails to R-related mailing lists. The advantage of this way of
sending data is that a potential helpeR is assured that when the
dput() output is copied and pasted into an R session, the structure of
that object is identical to the one on your computer.

Example:

set.seed(53490)
DF <- data.frame(x = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
                 y = rpois(4, 10))

> DF    # Don't send this...
  x  y
1 A  8
2 B  9
3 A 11
4 B 10
> str(DF)
'data.frame':   4 obs. of  2 variables:
 $ x: Factor w/ 2 levels "A","B": 1 2 1 2
 $ y: int  8 9 11 10
>
> dput(DF)    # Send the output of this
structure(list(x = structure(c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L), .Label = c("A",
"B"), class = "factor"), y = c(8L, 9L, 11L, 10L)), .Names = c("x",
"y"), row.names = c(NA, -4L), class = "data.frame")

If you copy and paste the output from dput() into your R session,
assign it to an object DF and type DF; str(DF), you should find that
it is identical to the output given above. In other words, there is no
ambiguity over whether or not x is a factor or a character vector.
The object you entered is identical to the one I sent.

You are now informed about dput(), and hopefully others are as well  :)

You're welcome, Brandon ;D

Dennis

However, my sense is that you could do most of this via vectorized code as functions themselves can be vectorized, e.g., `exp`, there is no need to use `vapply` to apply `exp` to each value, the function is already vectorized.

> vapply(1:3, exp, numeric(1))
[1]  2.718282  7.389056 20.085537

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to do calculations across at least two ordered dimensions, but the calculations should only use observations that have been specified. For example, if I have a j x k matrix, I want to take the product for all elements for j <= jj and k <= kk. That is, the product of everything to the left and up from the j, k element. But I might also want to take products for elements with j - 1 <= j <= j + 1 and k <= kk. That is, the product of elements within 1 row up and down and to the left of the j, k element.

With a matrix or array this may be straightforward, but I have data.frame with index variables j and k.

The following code does what I want, but it is terribly clunky. I'd rather not have to deal with keeping track of an elements position, as the formula jj + (n + (kk -1)) in the code only works because the indices in this case start from 1. I'd also like to easily express the filter as  a function argument.

> dt <- data.frame(j = rep(1:3, 3),
>            k = sort(rep(1:3, 3)),
>            y = runif(9))
>
> compute_prods <- function(data)
> {
>   n <- max(data$j)
>   out <- data
>
>   for(kk in min(data$k):max(data$k) ){
>     for(jj in min(data$j):max(data$j) ){
>       pos  <- (jj)  + n * (kk - 1)
>       these_rows <- filter_(out, paste0('j <=', jj, '&', 'k <=', kk))
>
>       out[pos, 'val'] <- prod(these_rows[ , 'y'], na.rm = T)
>     }
>   }
>   rm(jj, kk, pos)
>   return(out)
> }
>
> compute_prods(dt)

I looked at the tbl_cube options, but I don't think that will work without a mutate function, since I'm not collapsing the data. Another option might be to recast the data frame into matrix and then apply over both dimensions then reshape back to data frame. Also, the data in the example does not have other dimensions, but in reality I need to perform this operation within other dimensions (e.g. j and k will be nested within an ID variable).

Any ideas from the group are appreciated.

-Bradley
